cases.sentence: ___, которое он увидал у Ростовых, была Наташа.
cases.explain: «Первое лицо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The first person he saw in the house was Natásha. Even before he saw her, while taking off his cloak, he heard her. She was practicing solfa exercises in the music room. He knew that she had not sung since her illness, and so the sound of her voice surprised and delighted him. He opened the door softly and saw her, in the lilac dress she had worn at church, walking about the room singing. She had her back to him when he opened the door, but when, turning quickly, she saw his broad, surprised face, she blushed and came rapidly up to him.

cases.sentence: Я нынче так счастлива! ― сказала она с тем ___, которого уже давно не видел в ней Пьер. ― Вы знаете, Nicolas получил Георгиевский крест.
cases.explain: «прежним оживлением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “How glad I am you’ve come! I am so happy today,” she said, with the old animation Pierre had not seen in her for a long time. “You know Nicolas has received a St. George’s Cross? I am so proud of him.”

cases.sentence: Не будет он иметь против меня ___?
cases.explain: «злого чувства» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I don’t know myself,” Natásha answered quickly, “but I should not like to do anything you disapproved of. I believe in you completely. You don’t know how important you are to me, how much you’ve done for me. …” She spoke rapidly and did not notice how Pierre flushed at her words. “I saw in that same army order that he, Bolkónski” (she whispered the name hastily), “is in Russia, and in the army again. What do you think?”—she was speaking hurriedly, evidently afraid her strength might fail her—“Will he ever forgive me? Will he not always have a bitter feeling toward me? What do you think? What do you think?”

cases.sentence: ― Да вы ― вы, ― сказала она, с восторгом произнося это слово вы, ― ___.
cases.explain: «другое дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, you … you …” she said, uttering the word you rapturously—“that’s a different thing. I know no one kinder, more generous, or better than you; nobody could be! Had you not been there then, and now too, I don’t know what would have become of me, because …” Tears suddenly rose in her eyes, she turned away, lifted her music before her eyes, began singing again, and again began walking up and down the room.

cases.sentence: Петя был теперь красивый, румяный, ___ с толстыми, красными губами, похожий на Наташу.
cases.explain: «пятнадцатилетний мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Pétya was now a handsome rosy lad of fifteen with full red lips and resembled Natásha. He was preparing to enter the university, but he and his friend Obolénski had lately, in secret, agreed to join the hussars.

cases.sentence: — Князь Голицын ___ взял, — по-русски учится — il commence à devenir dangereux de parler français dans les rues.[617] становится опасным говорить по-французски на улицах.
cases.explain: «русского учителя» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “And have you heard?” Shinshín asked. “Prince Golítsyn has engaged a master to teach him Russian. It is becoming dangerous to speak French in the streets.”

cases.sentence: Я не знаю, я так далек от ___, но в теперешние времена никто за себя отвечать не может.
cases.explain: «военных вкусов» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh yes, the war,” he said. “No! What sort of warrior should I make? And yet everything is so strange, so strange! I can’t make it out. I don’t know, I am very far from having military tastes, but in these times no one can answer for himself.”

cases.explain: «великими силами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “The enemy has entered the borders of Russia with immense forces. He comes to despoil our beloved country.” Sónya read painstakingly in her high-pitched voice. The count listened with closed eyes, heaving abrupt sighs at certain passages.

cases.sentence: Он идет разорять любезное наше отечество», старательно читала Соня своим ___.
cases.explain: «тоненьким голоском» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “The enemy has entered the borders of Russia with immense forces. He comes to despoil our beloved country.” Sónya read painstakingly in her high-pitched voice. The count listened with closed eyes, heaving abrupt sighs at certain passages.

cases.sentence: — вскрикнул граф, открывая ___ и несколько раз прерываясь от сопенья, как будто к носу ему подносили стклянку с крепкою уксусною солью.
cases.explain: «мокрые глаза» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, that’s it!” cried the count, opening his moist eyes and sniffing repeatedly, as if a strong vinaigrette had been held to his nose; and he added, “Let the Emperor but say the word and we’ll sacrifice everything and begrudge nothing.”
